name: Machine Learning for Wireless Communications
description: Classification and regression: probabilistic classifiers, Bayes classifier, logistic regression. Non-probabilistic classifiers- K-nearest neighbors, discriminative and generative classifiers. Applications: i. 5G massive MIMO zero-forcing and MMSE receiver design ii. Detection in digital communication systems 2. Basics of reinforcement learning: dynamic programming, Monte-Carlo methods, temporal difference learning and Q-learning. Applications i. Q-learning for cross-layer resource allocation ii. Reinforcement learning-based joint scheduling of eMBB and URLLC in 5G networks 3. Basics of deep-learning: introduction to deep learning, neural networks, activation functions, loss functions and optimization, backpropagation and gradient descent, deep learning architectures (MLP, CNN, RNN) 5 convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and LSTMs, transfer learning and pretrained models, generative models (GANs, VAEs) applications: i. Deep learning for the physical layer ii. Deep learning for joint source-channel coding iii. Deep learning-based channel estimation 4. Closing comments: need and feasibility of ML in wireless, compute power requirement, where to deploy such algorithms (core/gNB/edge? ).
